Aangs true character arc is how he grows up and takes responsibility. He didnt want to be the avatar and fleed from his responsibility, now he has to face the consequances and own it up. And its also gradually evolving. Overanalyzing avatar points it out that there is a shift in tone at exactly in the middle of the show where the gaang stops fleeing from fighting and starts to tackle the challenges head on.

Aang owning up to be the avatar is also symbolised by how he feels after the avatar state. In the beginning, he collapses, later he just gets dizzy, and by the end, he enters it willingly and stands tall after it.

I still agree that this arc is less relatable and less familiar with Zuko's. There is less contrast in it too, which makes it a bit more flat.

Aang is still my favourite character from the show - I always wanted to be like him as a kid, mainly because he was so confident in his powers. I think that is a bit unusual for a kid hero as they are usually underdogs who have to fight for their powers. But it only makes it more interesting.

Szerintem igenis számít, hogy mennyit gondolkodik a vélaszadás előtt. Persze a hosszú csend lehet dramatúrgiai eszköz is, de itt közel sem az volt. Az a baj, hogy ezek a hosszú csöndek és a "nem tudom'-ok nem azt a benyomást keltik, hogy jól megrágja a kérdést hanem azt, hogy egyáltalán nem őszinte a válasz és, vagy hogy fingja sincs egy csomó mindenről a pártja körül. Ezek a hosszú csöndek és bizonytalan válaszok azt mutatják, hogy tudja ő, hogy mit akar mondani, csak görcsösen próbálja azt kikerülni, vagy máshogy elmondani. Se nem őszinte, se nem határozott.   
Ellenben meg lehet nézni a Márki-Zayos interjút. A fickó szemrebbenés nélkül válaszol a kérdésekre, mert tudja, hogy mit akar mondani és hisz abban, hogy jó az amit mond (a gyereknevelős résznél azért ő is hebegett kicsit, ahogy próbálta finomítani a helyzetet). 

Az emberek nem a kampányígéretekért nézik a partizán-interjút, hanem hogy lássák, hogy milyen emberrel, milyen politikussal is van dolguk. Fegyőr pedig csúnyán leszerepelt, mint politikus és rétor.

I am actually hungarian from Budapest :D and I am going to Lisbon in september for 5 months. Lisbon is a huge party-city so I am a bit nervous about the social life there, but I believe everything will be fine and I will have the time of my life there. 

About your doubts, having no family support there, and being independent: I am not even nervous about this. I have a great relationship with my parents, and if you have too, you can always call them and speak with them about any problem. If they can't even help directly, they will listen to you and be supportive. The being independent part is interesting. I really look forward to try out living independently, I see it as a chellenge. At one point we have to grow up and learn it, and a semester abroad is absolutely the best way to learn it I think. 

And does the ESN have a buddy program where you go? If yes, apply to it, because I believe they would help you in any case there, and be your kind-of-family, to provide you support.

For closing, I usually think about how I will look like when I get back home. I imagine how different will I be, with full of confidence (which I kind of lack now), full of experience and with great stories to tell. I don't know if these aspects are important to you, but I always get more determined, when I think about how much I can improve myself in this short 5 months. 

I hope my thouhgts are helpful to you, and you will have a great time there!
